to confluence in growth medium (0 D) and then shifted to differentiation
medium for a period of 5 Days. Cells were treated with T-Cap siRNA
duplex constructs and analyzed for RNA and protein expression using
Northern blots, real-time RT-PCR, and Western immunoblots. Addition-
ally, cDNA from T-Cap knockdown was compared with control in a multi-
well PCR-based array designed to provide pathway-focused gene expression
profiling. RESULTS: SiRNA treatment decreased T-Cap RNA and protein
expression in differentiating muscle cells. Levels of myostatin were subse-
quently increased, while decreases were observed in the myogenic regula-
tory factors MyoD and myogenin. SiRNA treatment also prevented
development of the normal phenotype of muscle cells in a dose-dependent
manner. Finally, statistically significant (p<0.05) differential expression of
key genes controlling cell cycle was observed. CONCLUSIONS/RELE-
VANCE: Our findings support the hypothesis that T-Cap knockdown with
RNA interference increases myostatin and impairs normal muscle cell dif-
ferentiation. This process likely occurs downstream of myostatin via repres-
son of myogenic regulatory factors, and cyclin-dependent kinases.

P07.045
Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Gene
Transfer Using Adeno-Associated Viral Vectors
Stimulates Skeletal Muscle Regeneration and
Enhances Muscle Function in mdx Mice Sonia
Messina, Mohammed Aguennouz, Anna Mazzeo, Alessandra Bitto,
Messina, Italy, Mauro Giacca, Trieste, Italy, Francesco Squadrito,
Giuseppe Vita, Messina, Italy
OBJECTIVE: Vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) is a major regu-
lator of physiological and pathological angiogenesis. We tested VEGF effect
on muscle function, histopathology, immunohistochemistry and biochemical
parameters in mdx and wild type mice. BACKGROUND: Several studies
support its role in myogenesis and in myoblast migration and survival.
Recently it has been reported that the delivery of VEGF using adeno-
ociated-virus (AAV) vectors reduces muscle damage and promotes mus-
cle regeneration in experimental models of muscle necrosis. DESIGN/
METHODS: We performed intramuscular administration into the biceps
and tibialis anterior muscles of AAV-VEGF or AAV-LacZ as controls. RE-
SULTS: One month after injection, AAV-VEGF treated muscles showed
augmented expression of VEGF (p<0.05) and VEGFR-2 (p<0.01) compared
to controls. VEGF treated mdx mice showed higher forelimb strength
{+19.5%, p<0.05) as well as higher strength normalised to weight (+14.9%,
p<0.05). At quantitative morphological evaluation of mdx mice, VEGF-
treated muscles showed a reduction of necrotic fibers area (p<0.05) and an
increase of small centrally nucleated fibers area (p<0.05). VEGF-treated
mdx mice muscle showed an increased number of cells positive for markers
of early and late regeneration, respectively myogenin and developmental
myosin heavy chain (p<0.05), and also an augmented capillary density in
regenerating fibers area (p<0.05). CONCLUSIONS/RELEVANCE: We
report the novel observation of a beneficial effect of VEGF in mdx mice
exerted mainly by a pro-regenerative and angiogenic effect. Further studies
are needed to better clarify the mechanisms of action of VEGF and there-
fore the possible therapeutic implications in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

disclose.
P07.046
Biased Usage of the T-Cell-Receptor (TCR) b-
Chain-Variable-Region (Vb) of CD4+ Peripheral-
Blood-Lymphocytes (PBL) in Patients with Stiff
Person Syndrome (SPS) Goran Rakocevic, Alexey
Shatunov, Raghavan Raju, Lev G. Goldfarb, Marinos C. Dalakas,
Bethesda, MD
OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether in SPS patients the CD4+ T cells
are clonally expanded, and therefore antigen-driven, using the
Complementarity-Determining-Region-3 (CDR3) spectratyping. BACK-
GROUND: SPS is an autoimmune disease mediated by antibodies against
GAD and other autoantigens in the GABAergic system. Activation of
autoantigen-reactive T cells bearing a specific type of TCR is closely associ-
ated with the development of an autoimmune disease. The involvement of
such cells in antibody production of SPS patients has not been explored.
DESIGN/METHODS: We performed CDR3 spectratyping in all TCR- Vb
families in the PBL of 12 anti-GAD-antibody-positive SPS patients and 5
healthy controls. Further, we isolated CD4+ T-lymphocytes from 7 of the
SPS patients and 5 controls and compared their TCR- Vb profile longitudi-
nally over a 12 month-period. RESULTS: All 24 TCR- Vb families in the
PBL of the SPS patients and the controls had a normal (Gaussian) distri-
bution. However, in the CD4+ T cell subsets of the SPS patients up tol2%
of the Vb families expressed a monoclonal pattern (one-peak) and 30% a
restricted (= 3 peaks) pattern, compared to 0 and 6% in the controls. The
most prominent restriction (= 50%) was observed in the Vb15, Vb19, Vb23
and Vb24 families. CDR3 spectratyping performed 12 months later demon-
strated persistence of clonal restrictions that differed from patient to pa-
“ent. Three SPS patients with the highest Vb restriction had a severe
disease and brittle IDDM. CONCLUSIONS/RELEVANCE: Clonal expan-
sions, selectively for the CD4+ T cell subset, were observed in SPS patients
suggesting activation of autoantigen-reactive T cells. Preferential usage of
certain Vb-chains persists over a 12-month period indicating a continuous
antigenic stimulation and antibody production. Correlation of CD4+ cell
clones with antibody titers and disease severity will be presented.
Supported by: NINDS.

close. Dr. Raju has nothing to disclose. Dr. Goldfarb has nothing to disclose. Dr. Dalakas

Association Analysis of the MAPT H1 Haplotype
and Subhaplotypes in Parkinson’s Disease Cyrus
Zabetian, Carolyn M. Hutter, Seattle, WA, Stewart Factor, At-
lanta, GA, John Nutt, Portland, OR, Donald Higgins, Albany, NY,
Alida Griffith, Kirkland, WA, John Roberts, Seattle, WA, Berta
Leis, Kirkland, WA, Denise M. Kay, Albany, NY, Dora Yearout,
Seattle, WA, Jennifer S. Montimurro, Albany, NY, Karen L.
Edwards, Ali Samiti, Seattle, WA, Haydeh Payami, Albany, NY
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether common variation within the
microtubule-associated protein tau (MAPT) gene is a risk factor for Parkin-
son’s disease (PD). BACKGROUND: An inversion polymorphism of ~900
kb on chromosome 17q21 which includes the MAPT gene defines two hap-
lotype clades, H1 and H2, which do not recombine. Several small case-
control studies have observed a marginally significant excess of the H1/H1
diplotype among PD patients. An analysis of H1 subhaplotypes in a Norwe-
gian PD cohort refined the association to a region spanning exons 1-4 of
MAPT. DESIGN/METHODS: The study population consisted of 1,762 PD
patients and 2,064 controls of self-defined ‘Caucasian’ ancestry recruited
from multiple centers across North America. We genotyped these individu-
als for one single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP; rs1800547) that differen-
tiates the Hl and H2 haplotype clades and four SNPs that define H1-
specific subhaplotypes previously reported to associate with PD or other
neurodegenerative disorders. RESULTS: After adjusting for age, sex, and
site we observed a robust association between the H1/H1 diplotype and PD
risk (odds ratio for HI/H1 vs. HI/H2 and H2/H2, 1.46; 95% CI, 1.26-1.69;
p=7 X 1077). An excess of HI/H1 was observed in patients with and
without a family history of PD, and in both early (<50 years) and late onset
(>50 years) disease. However, no significant association was seen for any of
the H1 subhaplotypes of interest. This included the two locus (rs242562,
rs2435207) subhaplotype previously reported to narrow the disease interval
to a 90 kb region of MAPT. CONCLUSIONS/RELEVANCE: Our data
provide strong evidence that the H1 haplotype clade, which includes MAPT
and several other genes, is a risk factor for PD. However, we believe that
attributing this finding to variants within a specific region of MAPT is
premature.
Supported by: Michael J. Fox Foundation, Department of Veterans Af-
fairs, and National Institutes of Health.
